ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When you say 'leaf' and 'leave' aloud, what is the last sound of 'leave'? (1 mark)
   A. /d/
   B. /t/
   C. /v/
   D. /f/

2. Which word ends with the sound /v/? (1 mark)
   A. leaf
   B. proof
   C. leave
   D. half

3. What should you do before using a website for facts? (1 mark)
   A. Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   B. Share your address
   C. Copy it without reading
   D. Believe everything

4. Which word means 'to make a place pretty with balloons and ribbons'? (1 mark)
   A. celebrate
   B. graduate
   C. attend
   D. decorate

5. Which word has the same vowel sound as 'bird'? (1 mark)
   A. time
   B. turn
   C. card
   D. toy

6. A simile compares two things using (1 mark)
   A. if or then
   B. who or which
   C. but or and
   D. like or as

7. A direct question is one whose answer (1 mark)
   A. has no words
   B. is not in the text
   C. is a joke
   D. is written in the text

8. Which word stays the same in the plural? (1 mark)
   A. sheep
   B. hen
   C. cow
   D. goat

9. In a plan for a story, the middle usually tells (1 mark)
   A. only the title
   B. the last sentence
   C. what happens
   D. the name of the school

10. Which part of a composition tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The conclusion
   B. The introduction
   C. The title only
   D. The body

11. Reading a text again more slowly to understand it well is called (1 mark)
   A. scanning
   B. intensive reading
   C. copying
   D. silent singing

12. What is a good way to find the meaning of an unknown word in a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the passage
   B. Guess without reading
   C. Read the sentences around it for clues
   D. Ask a stranger

13. Which word has a silent b? (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. bat
   C. ribbon
   D. lamb

14. Which letter is a tail letter? (1 mark)
   A. m
   B. o
   C. t
   D. g

15. First aid words: Which word has the sound /ɒ/? (1 mark)
   A. pain
   B. snake
   C. doctor
   D. bite

16. In which direction does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. South
   D. East

17. On most maps, north is at the (1 mark)
   A. left
   B. bottom
   C. right
   D. top

18. Which word begins the greeting in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Sincerely
   B. Yours
   C. Faithfully
   D. Dear

19. Listening and diet: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I would like to be a nurse.
   B. I would like be a nurse.
   C. I would like to being a nurse.
   D. I would likes to be a nurse.

20. Which is a sentence starter for sharing a story? (1 mark)
   A. Yours faithfully...
   B. My favourite part was...
   C. To whom it may concern...
   D. Dear Sir...

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write three sentences about a car near a bridge using one subject pronoun, one object pronoun and one possessive pronoun. (3 marks)

22. Write two sentences beginning 'I would like to be' and give a reason in each. (3 marks)

23. Write directions to walk from the school to the market on the map in the lesson. (3 marks)

24. Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate. (2 marks)

25. State three materials you can read for pleasure. (3 marks)

26. Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

27. Explain how you can feel the difference between /t/ and /d/ using your throat. (2 marks)

28. Read: 'Juma asked his mother to add vegetables to his lunch.' Say why Juma did this, using the story 'A Pot of Vegetables'. (2 marks)

29. Write an introduction of two sentences for the topic 'A day I enjoyed'. (2 marks)

30. Explain how to use the five-finger test. (3 marks)

31. Write an invitation of three sentences to a wedding or birthday party, using 'invite' and 'decorate'. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — /v/
   Leave ends with the voiced sound /v/.

2. C — leave
   Leave ends with /v/. Leaf, half and proof end with /f/.

3. A — Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   Checking a second source shows whether the fact is correct.

4. D — decorate
   To decorate is to make a place look pretty.

5. B — turn
   Bird and turn both have /ɜː/.

6. D — like or as
   A simile uses like or as, for example as brave as a lion.

7. D — is written in the text
   Direct answers are stated plainly in the text.

8. A — sheep
   Sheep is both singular and plural.

9. C — what happens
   The middle tells the events, including any problem.

10. B — The introduction
   The introduction sets the scene.

11. B — intensive reading
   Intensive reading means careful, slow reading.

12. C — Read the sentences around it for clues
   Context clues help you understand new words.

13. D — lamb
   In lamb the b is not pronounced.

14. D — g
   G hangs below the line.

15. C — doctor
   Doctor has the short vowel /ɒ/.

16. D — East
   The sun rises in the east.

17. D — top
   North is shown at the top of a map.

18. D — Dear
   Friendly letters begin with Dear and the name.

19. A — I would like to be a nurse.
   The pattern is would like to be + noun phrase.

20. B — My favourite part was...
   It helps you tell what you liked.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has bright head lights. The bridge protects us. The car is theirs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: I would like to be a doctor because I want to help sick people. I would like to be a runner because I love sport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence with reason, and 1 for accuracy.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk east to the roundabout, go straight east across the foot bridge and you will reach the market.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for east, 1 mark for the roundabout and 1 mark for the foot bridge and market.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put your fingers on your throat and say the sounds. You feel a buzz with /d/ because it is voiced, but no buzz with /t/, which is whispered.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the buzz with /d/, 1 mark for no buzz with /t/.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mama Zuri told him vegetables give vitamins that protect the body from sickness, so he wanted to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for vitamins or protection and 1 mark for linking to Juma.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: It was a sunny Sunday in Kisumu. My family went to the lake for a picnic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for when or where and 1 mark for who or what.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: I invite you to my sister's wedding on Saturday. We will decorate the hall with flowers. Please come at ten o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.
